situation:
You are the director of restaurant training for COPPER CREEK CHICKEN, a chicken sandwich chain of sixty-four stores. A new president (judge) took over eight months ago after two years of falling sales and closed stores, and is rebuilding the menu around one premium sandwich.

The sandwich is hand-breaded and pressure-fried to a narrow temperature window, so no store may sell it until its crew is certified. Sixty-four stores must certify before the summer, and the president (judge) has promised franchise operators a launch date they have already begun advertising to their own guests.

The cheapest path is a two-hour online course from an outside training vendor, taken on shift on a store tablet. It certifies every crew in three weeks and costs little, but nobody watches a cook actually pull a basket, and the vendor stores each crew member's name, hours and test records on its own servers under terms the company has not reviewed.

The other path sends two crew from every store to a regional kitchen for two days with a company trainer who watches each cook and signs them off. It protects the sandwich in a chain that cannot afford another bad quarter, but travel and wages run far higher, and certification finishes six weeks past the date operators are advertising.

The president (judge) has asked you to recommend one certification path and to explain what it means for the guests the chain is trying to win back. The president (judge) will greet you, listen to your recommendation and ask a few questions, and will thank you when the presentation is finished.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the president (judge) of COPPER CREEK CHICKEN. Business background is the same as the situation above. You came in after two bad years, you have staked the turnaround on one premium sandwich, and you have given franchise operators a launch date they are already advertising to their guests.

You want the director of restaurant training to recommend either the two-hour online course from the outside training vendor or the two days at a regional kitchen with a company trainer, and to explain what that choice means for the guests the chain is trying to win back.

During the presentation you are to ask the following questions of each participant:
judgeQuestions: What do we give up by not taking the other path?
Who would notice first if the certification we choose is not enough?
